newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo says hyperinflation being beaten.
newsitem.headline: New Congo says hyperinflation being beaten.

text.p: Hyperinflation which ravaged Mobutu Sese Seko's Zaire has been stopped in its tracks since he fled and Laurent Kabila took over, the new finance minister said on Thursday.
"Latest statistics show hyperinflation has fallen from 900 percent in April to minus 20 percent in May," Mawapanga Mwana Nanga told a news conference.

In a move to quell growing unrest at wages that have remained unpaid for six months, he also promised civil servants would get their money by June 25 -- even though the new government had found the state coffers empty.
"We will pay one month's salary and after that the civil servants will be paid each month," he said.
He said authorities had seized billions of Zaires, the unchanged name of the currency, from speculators hoping to make a quick buck from out-of-kilter regional exchange rates.

Because they are in larger-value notes used only in the southeast of the vast country, the 60 billion zaires are worth nothing in the capital Kinshasa but around $350,000 in the second city Lubumbashi, the copper capital.
To prevent people making money out of the money printed freely by the previous regime, transporting the larger notes -- known as "prostates" in a jibe at Mobutu's cancer -- around Congo is illegal.
Mawapanga said the notes were confiscated in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi. He did not say if the traffickers had been caught.
Analysts say restoring confidence in the currency and paying state employees are Kabila's best way to winning the support of a population that has high expectations after three decades of misrule.
Mawapanga said the new Congo Franc would replace the Zaire in a planned monetary reform and the notes would start to be printed soon.
